To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU capacity triage: ACME commit window (weekly check)

Team —

Quick sync request for this week. ACME is moving to a firm close window (finance expects signature by Jul 20) and they’ve signaled 3x reserved slots for Q3 if we can guarantee start-of-service by Aug 1. I pulled a preliminary heatmap (attached) and a slot request template.

Asks:
- Laura: can you confirm which deals in the close plan will convert to reserved slots (quick yes/no + expected start date)? Please include HubSpot deal IDs.
- Ben/Karthik: what is realistic lead time to stand up 3x 48GB A100 reserved nodes in Dedicated vs. bursting from non-prod? Any infra constraints or rollback controls we should bake into the canary?
- Priyom: can you validate if finance can accelerate the runway for a mid-July invoice cycle if ACME asks for an earlier start?

Attachments:
- Q3_pipeline_heatmap.xlsx (summary by close week)
- slot_request_form.pdf (required fields for infra/procurement)

I’d like short replies by EOD tomorrow so we can decide whether to surface this in Sales-Finance-Infra on Thursday.

— Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: GPU capacity triage: ACME commit window (weekly check)

Thanks, Jasmine — quick update from Sales forecast:

- ACME (ACME-2026-Q3-EXPAND-77): Sales confidence moved to 85% after legal excepted SOW; target start-of-service request: 2026-08-01.
- Other near-term deals that might request reserved capacity this quarter: Nimbus Health (50% confidence, smaller footprint), CloudForge (60%).

Per ACME: they want 3 reserved slots (48GB) for production and 1 slot for canary. If we confirm start-of-service by Aug 1 they will sign by Jul 20 (linked the deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2026-Q3-EXPAND-77).

I attached a small calc sheet that maps token estimates to slot-days. Short answer to your asks: yes, ACME should convert if infra can meet the start date; will confirm signature timeline with Sarah K.

— Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: GPU capacity triage: ACME commit window (weekly check)

Appreciate the heads-up. From infra reality check:

- Dedicated provisioning timeline: building three 48GB A100 reserved nodes end-to-end (procurement, racking, image bake, autoscale config, SLA) is ~3 weeks if we can reuse existing rack capacity. If hardware needs to be ordered, add 4–6 weeks.
- Short-term options:
  * Burst from non-prod: we can carve 20% of non-prod pools between Jul 12–20 for a soft canary; this requires approvals and will impact internal test coverage.
  * Quantization fallback: encourage a 4-bit quantized model variant for canary to reduce memory live set by ~30% so startup can fit into smaller slots.
  * Canary policy: recommend a 2-week canary with automatic rollback to hosted API if error rates exceed 2% or P50 latency > 250ms.

Actionable ask for Sales: confirm exact concurrency and SLA expectation during canary vs GA. For example: do they expect steady concurrency of 250 rps or peak bursts at 1k? That drives whether 3x slots is sufficient or we should request additional burst credits.

I’ll open an infra ticket to model the slot fit and list what we can reassign from non-prod.

— Ben Carter
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Thanks everyone — short plan and owners so we can move before Thursday’s cross-functional readout:

- Laura: confirm ACME signature timeline with Sarah K and provide final HubSpot update by Mon 7/13. (If they push signature past Jul 20, call it out in the update.)
- Ben: infra ticket (INF-7821) created to evaluate carving 20% non-prod and to model 3x 48GB slot fit + quantized fallback by Tue 7/14.
- Karthik: prepare canary routing policy and rollback SLO draft; coordinate with Ben on autoscale knobs.
- Priyom: quick finance check — can we move invoice/runway if ACME requests start by Aug 1 and AtlasCloud asks for expedited billing? Flag by EOD Mon 7/13.
- Procurement (AtlasCloud): Jasmine to send PO intent if Sales confirms — thanks for the expedited stub.

I’ll prepare a one-pager for Thursday’s readout summarizing runway impact, slot risk, and cost delta for expedited provisioning.

Cheers,
